entries.reason: DecodeStage remains the Fovea host owner of probe revalidation, codec capability negotiation, generic-plus-backend working-set admission, prepared-state lifecycle, blocking execution, cancellation and aggregate diagnostics. Swift 6.4 async defer now makes subscription release, preparation discard and priority-control completion structurally unavoidable without adding mutable state or a new responsibility. These operations still form one permit, prepared-state and failure transaction; splitting before a second production backend demonstrates a stable collaborator would duplicate admission ordering, cancellation mapping or prepared-state cleanup.

public codec capability and conservative resource admission
decode executor, permit and prepared-state lifecycle
aggregate diagnostics, failure mapping and cancellation

entries.reason: SharedTaskRegistry is one actor state machine covering subscription cohorts, effective priority, orphan handoff leases and cancellation tombstones. The cancellation lease now stores an absolute monotonic expiry and performs lazy expiry on subscribe, so timer scheduling is only a cleanup optimization rather than a correctness dependency. Keeping entry, tombstone, lease identity, completion and join transitions in one actor preserves a reviewable linearization boundary; splitting storage from transitions would weaken the proof and make ABA prevention harder to audit.

modules.reason: FoveaCore is the Fovea-owned policy and orchestration layer for request identity, geometry, resource admission, fetch/decode execution, rendered caching, namespace lifecycle, shared work and diagnostics. Its absolute file count is unchanged at 54; its repository source share rose when ImageCraft and Akashic production directories were physically removed. The current files preserve one-way dependencies and no reviewed policy family can yet move without importing FoveaCore back or duplicating identity, authority or transaction semantics.
